reviews.reasoning: Re-derived, not accepted. Ps 132 is an identity psalm (web_mt_offset_map.json: rule identity, 18 WEB verses = 18 MT verses, web_title true), so web:Ps.132.0 = oshb:Ps.132.1 and web:Ps.132.1 = oshb:Ps.132.1 both hold; the row's title pairing is arithmetically correct and no shift dual-cite is owed. All 4 Hebrew runs in this row collate at byte tier against the refs they carry (collate.py --json over the cluster: 12 runs, status GREEN, 0 below byte). Token counts from verse_map_oshb.json: Ps.132.1 splits into 8 whitespace tokens, tokens 1-2 being the genre label and token 5 the David-word, so the row's quoted plea is 3 tokens and its 'third word' is the David-word exactly as stated. The no-name claim is confirmed twice independently of the row: psalm_device_inventory.json superscriptions/132 carries 2 labels, shir and shir_hammaalot, with le_david present at superscriptions/133 and absent here, and the strategy's §11 p22 erratum records le_david = 73 psalms with 132 excluded on exactly this ground (the David-word read as content, not attribution). Far seam verified from WEB bytes rather than from the row: the opening curly mark is character 1 of web:Ps.132.3, the closing mark is the final character of web:Ps.132.5 (index 76 of 76, 0 characters follow it), web:Ps.132.6 carries 0 quotation marks, and the next opening mark is character 1 of web:Ps.132.7 - all three substrate statements hold. The rejected_alternative's syntactic warrant is byte-true: oshb:Ps.132.2 opens with the relativizer אֲשֶׁ֣ר at token 1 before the oath verb at token 2, so 132:1 has no independent close. Selah absence is true and span-scoped (pmarks_Ps.json selah has 71 keys, 0 of them in Ps 132-134); marks is empty at 0 keys and the row makes no pe/samekh claim in either direction. Confidence high is calibrated. Two observations, not defects: (1) the 3-token Hebrew clip at oshb:Ps.132.1 is glossed by the whole of web:Ps.132.1 including the affliction colon, a quote/gloss span widening that recurs in 5 of this cluster's 6 rows while the same writer cuts to parity at oshb:Ps.132.8 - it reads as a book-wide author-wave parity item, not a row defect; (2) check_universals flags 'carries no name' for want of an adjacent digit-bearing count, but the claim is byte-true and inventory-confirmed as above.

The mechanical layer is sound: the four Ps 132 rows tile Ps.132.1-Ps.132.18 exactly (check_tiling: 18 expected, 18 covered, 0 problems), the row's single Hebrew run collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.132.8, and it is the one quote/gloss pair in the cluster cut to the same colon on both sides. The WEB quotation census the row describes is also accurate: web:Ps.132.7 carries exactly 1 opening and 1 closing mark with the closing mark as its final character, while web:Ps.132.6 and web:Ps.132.8 carry 0. The person analysis is what fails, and it fails in both the rationale and the rejected_alternative. Ps 132:6-7 does not address Yahweh: across its 11 tokens 0 carry a second-person form - 132:6 is 1cp narration with 2 tokens taking a 3fs object suffix, and 132:7 refers to God in the third person - against 3 second-person tokens in 132:8, so the reason given for rejecting a 132:7|8 split is false, and the row's own second substrate signal states the opposite of its own rejected_alternative. The rival is not taste: the row policy lists speaker/addressee shifts first among tier-1 internal-seam drivers, and 132:8 adds an imperative opening. I am not asserting the span is wrong - 132:6-10 as the community's movement is defensible, and a 2-verse plus 3-verse split would fall below the strophe norm of roughly 4-8 verses - but the warrant that kills the rival must be replaced by one that survives the same byte check. Two further observations: this is the only row of the 6 that omits the span-scoped selah-absence signal its 4 siblings carry, and the absence would be true (0 selah keys in Ps 132-134), so the disclosure is asymmetric within one psalm; and confidence high is not supported while the stated unifying warrant is contradicted by the bytes.

challenges.claim: The row's unifying warrant and its rejected_alternative both assert that Ps 132:6-7 is addressed to Yahweh in the second person, but those verses speak of God only in the third person, so the sole stated reason for rejecting the tier-1 addressee-shift seam at 132:7|8 is false and self-contradicted by the row's own substrate signal.
challenges.evidence: Ps 132 is an identity psalm (web_mt_offset_map.json), so web:Ps.132.7 = oshb:Ps.132.7 and web:Ps.132.8 = oshb:Ps.132.8. Byte-spliced from verse_map_oshb.json: oshb:Ps.132.7 tokens 2 and 5 are לְמִשְׁכְּנוֹתָ֑יו and רַגְלָֽיו, both carrying the 3ms pronominal suffix (2 tokens, unit = tokens); oshb:Ps.132.8 carries 3 second-person tokens - לִמְנוּחָתֶ֑ךָ (token 3) and עֻזֶּֽךָ (token 6) with the 2ms suffix, plus the independent 2ms pronoun אַ֝תָּ֗ה (token 4). Second-person reference to Yahweh in this psalm begins at 132:8 and is absent from 132:6-7: a token scan of oshb:Ps.132.6-Ps.132.7 returns 0 second-person forms in 11 tokens. Both witnesses agree - WEB has “We will worship at his footstool.” (web:Ps.132.7) against “Arise, Yahweh, into your resting place, you, and the ark of your strength.” (web:Ps.132.8), and “Behold, we heard of it in Ephrathah. We found it in the field of Jaar.” (web:Ps.132.6) has no addressee at all. The row's own observed_substrate_signals entry states that second-person imperative address to Yahweh begins at web:Ps.132.8, which cannot stand beside its rejected_alternative's statement that the vow and the petition both remain addressed to the same second-person Yahweh. A replacement warrant must pass this same byte check.

reviews.reasoning: The seam the row chooses is genuinely byte-warranted, and I re-derived it without using the row's argument: oshb:Ps.132.13 carries the 3ms אִ֝וָּ֗הּ and oshb:Ps.132.14 answers with the 1cs אִוִּתִֽיהָ - one root in two voices across 13|14 - which is stronger evidence for the row's seam than the WEB punctuation it actually cites, and the row does not use it. The row's Hebrew run collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.132.11, refs mirror clean (check_refs_mirror: 0 flags), and confidence medium is the right calibration for a seam with a live rival. Two defects nevertheless. First, the substrate signal invokes a byte comparison of the two oath verbs without naming the tier at which they agree, and they do not agree at byte, nfd or accent_stripped - only at skeleton, which is the one tier that discards the vocalization a form claim depends on. Second, the same signal misstates where the divine-oath quotation closes, contradicting the row's own rationale. Neither defect touches the span, which I would keep; both touch evidence fields that a downstream re-derivation will fail. Noted for the seam pair, not filed here: the cross-seam anaphora and repetition running from 132:12 into 132:14-18 is filed against the row that opens at 132:14, and any cure is one edit installed on both rows at the 132:13|14 seam.

challenges.claim: The substrate signal offers a byte comparison of the oath verbs at 132:2 and 132:11 as warrant for the same inflected form, but the two forms are unequal at byte, nfd and accent_stripped tier and agree only at skeleton, and no tier is named.
challenges.evidence: Byte-spliced from verse_map_oshb.json (Ps 132 is identity, so web:Ps.132.2 = oshb:Ps.132.2): oshb:Ps.132.2 token 2 = נִ֭שְׁבַּע (10 codepoints, carrying U+05AD at position 3); oshb:Ps.132.11 token 1 = נִשְׁבַּֽע (10 codepoints, carrying U+05BD at position 9). ps_lib equality over the two spliced tokens: byte False, nfd False, accent_stripped False, skeleton True. accent_stripped fails because it strips U+0591-U+05AF only and therefore retains the meteg at 132:11 - exactly the encoding note the toolkit records. The substantive claim survives (the vowel pointing is identical; the two differ only in accent and meteg), so the cure is to name the tier, not to drop the signal. Two related gaps in the same row: 1 of the 2 compared forms is left unquoted here (the 132:2 form) although the claim is about verse_map_oshb.json text of both verses, and boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Ps.132.2 with no oshb: ref for it.

challenges.claim: The substrate signal states that the divine-oath quotation closes mid-132:12, which contradicts both the row's own rationale and the WEB bytes, where the closing mark is the verse's final character.
challenges.evidence: web:Ps.132.12 is 135 characters long; its closing curly mark stands at index 134 with 0 characters following it (“their children also will sit on your throne forever more.”, web:Ps.132.12). The row's rationale states the quotation runs through 132:12's close, which is the accurate description; the signal contradicts it. What is genuinely mid-verse is the OPENING mark at web:Ps.132.11, which is not that verse's first character - the quotation opens after “He will not turn from it:” (web:Ps.132.11). Census over Ps 132 (unit = verses): 4 verses carry an opening mark (132:3, 132:7, 132:11, 132:14) and 4 carry a closing mark (132:5, 132:7, 132:12, 132:18); of the 4 closing marks, 4 stand as the final character of their verse and 0 stand mid-verse. Left uncorrected, the signal implies unquoted material inside 132:12 and so implies a seam the bytes do not support.

reviews.reasoning: The row's positive warrant is real and byte-checkable: oshb:Ps.132.14 opens the oracle with first-person forms against the third-person report of oshb:Ps.132.13, and the closing curly mark is the final character of web:Ps.132.18 (index 75 of 75, 0 characters follow), so the oracle does close with the psalm. The single Hebrew run collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.132.14; unit_type strophe is in the controlled vocabulary; the selah absence is true (0 selah keys in Ps 132-134); the span closes the psalm's exact tiling. What the row does not do is disclose the cohesion running the other way across its own opening seam. Zion is named once in the psalm, at 132:13, one verse outside the span, and the oracle then depends on that antecedent through a chain of feminine anaphors, while a byte-identical two-token phrase stands on both sides of 132:13. Under the campaign's cross-seam cohesion standard those argue continuity against the row unless disclosed, and the row's rejected_alternative weighs only the thematic overlap ('both concern Zion's election'), not the grammatical dependency. I would not move the seam - the voice pivot is the stronger driver - but the disclosure is owed, and it is one edit installed on both rows sharing 132:13|14. Confidence high is otherwise defensible.

challenges.claim: The row opens one verse after the psalm's 1 naming of Zion and leaves 4 feminine-suffixed tokens in 132:15-16 plus the locative at 132:17 dependent on an antecedent outside its span, and it discloses neither that dependency nor the byte-identical phrase shared by 132:12 and 132:14 across the same seam.
challenges.evidence: Ps 132 is identity, so web:Ps.132.V = oshb:Ps.132.V throughout. A skeleton search for the Zion spelling over oshb:Ps.132.14-Ps.132.18 returns 0 verses; oshb:Ps.132.13 token 4 = בְּצִיּ֑וֹן is the psalm's only occurrence. Tokens bearing a 3fs pronominal suffix in oshb:Ps.132.15-Ps.132.16: 4 (unit = tokens) - צֵ֭ידָהּ and אֶ֝בְיוֹנֶ֗יהָ at 132:15, וְֽ֭כֹהֲנֶיהָ and וַ֝חֲסִידֶ֗יהָ at 132:16 - all byte-spliced from verse_map_oshb.json. I will satisfy her poor with bread.” (web:Ps.132.15) and “I will also clothe her priests with salvation.” (web:Ps.132.16) have their feminine referent supplied only by “For Yahweh has chosen Zion. Separately, the two-token phrase עֲדֵי עַ֑ד stands at oshb:Ps.132.12 tokens 10-11 and at oshb:Ps.132.14 tokens 3-4, equal at byte, nfd, accent_stripped and skeleton tier (10 codepoints each) - a byte-true repetition straddling the 132:13|14 seam. The cure is a disclosure on both rows of that seam, not a span change.

reviews.reasoning: Both Hebrew runs collate at byte tier against oshb:Ps.133.1. The title claim is verified from bytes rather than from the row: verse_map_oshb.json Ps.133.1 splits into 12 whitespace tokens with the David-word at token 3, immediately after the 2 genre-label tokens; psalm_device_inventory.json superscriptions/133 lists le_david alongside shir and shir_hammaalot, and WEB agrees, rendering the title “A Song of Ascents. By David.” (web:Ps.133.0) against 132's bare “A Song of Ascents.” (web:Ps.132.0) - so the contrast the row draws holds in both witnesses. Indivisibility checks out: Ps 133 carries 0 curly quotation marks across its 3 verses, 0 vocatives and 0 second-person forms, and 133:2 and 133:3 both open with a comparison particle, so the rejected_alternative's one-grammatical-frame warrant is byte-true rather than aesthetic. whole_psalm is the correct controlled-vocabulary type: the row policy assigns one whole_psalm row to short indivisible psalms of roughly 8 verses or fewer and names 133 among its examples; at 3 verses the row cannot be split without padding. Selah absence true (0 selah keys in Ps 133), no K/Q in the psalm (pmarks kq has 65 keys, 0 in Ps 132-134), and the 2 paseq segs at 133:2 and 133:3 are seg-layer, not quotable verse text, and are correctly not claimed. Confidence high is calibrated. Two observations, not defects: the rationale's opening citation is duplicated - the same parenthetical stands twice consecutively and 3 times in the field - and the phrase 'the same word' for the David-word at 132:1 and 133:1 is exact at accent_stripped and skeleton tier but not at byte or nfd (accents differ), so a tier should be named if that phrase survives the author wave.

Most of this row verifies, and one claim verifies more strongly than it is stated: the 2 title tokens of oshb:Ps.134.1 are byte-identical to those of oshb:Ps.132.1 (21 codepoints, equal at byte, nfd, accent_stripped and skeleton), not merely a repetition of wording, and psalm_device_inventory.json gives both psalms labels shir and shir_hammaalot with le_david for neither, while WEB renders both titles “A Song of Ascents.” (web:Ps.134.0). The addressee analysis is byte-true: 2mp imperative forms in 134:1-2 against the 2ms object suffix in 134:3. The Hebrew run collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.134.3; whole_psalm is right for a 3-verse psalm that the row policy names as an example; selah absence is true (0 selah keys) and the 1 paseq seg at 134:1 is seg-layer and correctly unclaimed; 0 K/Q notes fall in this psalm. The defect is evidentiary rather than factual: the row's cohesion warrant is a reversal in the direction of blessing, and that reversal lives only in the Hebrew root chain, which the row quotes for one of its three members while quoting a WEB rendering that conceals the other two. Confidence high is otherwise fine, since the unit is settled by the short-psalm rule independently of this warrant.

challenges.claim: The row argues the psalm's unity from a reversal in the direction of blessing but supplies original-language evidence for only the third of the 3 blessing verbs, and the WEB it quotes renders the first 2 as praise, so the device the row relies on is not visible in the evidence it cites.
challenges.evidence: Ps 134 is an identity psalm (web_mt_offset_map.json), so web:Ps.134.V = oshb:Ps.134.V. Byte-spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, the blessing root stands as 3 tokens in the psalm, 1 per verse (unit = tokens): בָּרֲכ֣וּ at oshb:Ps.134.1 token 4, וּ֝בָרֲכוּ at oshb:Ps.134.2 token 4, and יְבָרֶכְךָ֣ at oshb:Ps.134.3 token 1; the first 2 are 2mp imperatives directed at the servants and the third is a 3ms form carrying the 2ms object suffix, which is precisely the reversal the row claims. WEB does not show it: “Praise Yahweh, all you servants of Yahweh” (web:Ps.134.1) and “Lift up your hands in the sanctuary. Praise Yahweh!” (web:Ps.134.2) against “May Yahweh bless you from Zion” (web:Ps.134.3) - 1 of the 3 rendered with the blessing verb. The row quotes Hebrew for oshb:Ps.134.3 only, and boundary_evidence_refs carries no oshb: ref for 134:2 at all (134:1's MT ref enters only through the title pairing). The cure is to quote the first 2 tokens and cite their MT refs, since the argument leans on English that renders the root away.
